senses.definition: A substance that is harmful or lethal to a living organism when ingested.
examples: We used a poison to kill the weeds.

senses.definition: (figuratively) Anything harmful to a person or thing.

quotes.text:

senses.definition: (informal, idiomatic) An alcoholic drink. (Mainly in the phrases "name your poison" and "what's your poison?")
examples:
— What's your poison?
— I'll have a glass of whiskey.

senses.definition: (chemistry) Any substance that inhibits catalytic activity.

quotes.text: The temperature effect of poisons. The influence of poison on the catalyst can be different with the change of reaction conditions.

senses.definition: (transitive) To use poison to kill or paralyse (somebody).
(transitive) To pollute; to cause to become poisonous.
examples: That factory is poisoning the river.

senses.definition: (transitive) To cause to become much worse.
examples: He poisoned the mood in the room with his non-stop criticism.

senses.definition: (transitive) To cause (someone) to hate or to have unfair negative opinions.
examples: She's poisoned him against all his old friends.

senses.definition: (chemistry) To inhibit the catalytic activity of.
(transitive, computing) To place false or malicious data into (a cache, etc.) as part of an exploit.

quotes.text: In this technique, the hacker poisons the cache to launch malware into Web pages.
